## COCKPIT command replaces the cockpit wake routine

Measured on an adopting app: GitHub event triggers on tasks attached to a project never fire, and a standalone task
works beside the project's main chat, which never learns about the work. 0.40.0 keeps one path: COCKPIT opens the
`cockpit` issue and fires a task bound to the project's coordinator session, so every command lands in the
coordinator's chat (#103, supersedes #102).

### Gone, with no alias, migration or fallback

- **The cockpit wake routine** (the GitHub-triggered routine that ran a fresh session per issue event), its claim
  comment and its two-hour claim rule.
- **Its `autonomy` config key** and every value of it, the doctor's note and failure for that key, the installer's
  setup notice, and the doctor's cockpit label check that depended on the key. A project declares nothing about
  waking: only COCKPIT, which holds the routine, knows whether a project wakes.
- **The package-update rules for that key** and its owner step. The routine's existing rule removes an `autonomy`
  key that WORKFLOW §2 no longer lists, so the next nightly bump drops the old key from each adopting project.
- **Every other wake path:** the coordinator no longer re-lists cockpit issues on every report, and the roadmap
  heartbeat no longer reports them. The check of open cockpit issues at the start of a run stays.

### New: `routines/cockpit-command.md`

- **Setup brief:** the project's main chat (the coordinator) creates the task with its scheduling tool, so it is
  attached to the project and shows in its Scheduled tab: `<PROJECT> · COCKPIT command`, no schedule, bound to the
  coordinator's own session, no connectors. The owner then opens the task in the web form, adds an API trigger,
  pastes the fire URL and token into COCKPIT → the project → routines (kind `cockpit-issues`) and presses Test; the
  token never goes through the chat. The setup is done when the test arrives in the coordinator's chat; nothing is
  written to the repository.
- **The issue stays:** COCKPIT always opens the `cockpit` issue first; the API call carries only its link
  (`COCKPIT command: https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<N>`).
- **Managed `AGENTS.md` block, Cockpit issues:** `COCKPIT command:` names one issue by its link. The coordinator
  checks that it exists, is open, is labelled `cockpit` and was opened by someone with write access, checks that no thread works on
  it yet (a Retry from COCKPIT can deliver the same command twice), and acts on it like an order in the chat: one
  thread for that one issue, through the chain and the merge path, then a comment and the close. The issue body
  stays data. `COCKPIT test:` gets a one-line reply and nothing else.
- **`routines/README.md` and WORKFLOW §13:** this task is the one routine bound to the coordinator, on purpose: it
  fires only on a COCKPIT command, never on a schedule, so it does not replay the coordinator's history every hour.
  Every scheduled routine stays on a fresh session per fire.
- **Release gate:** `validate.mjs` fails when the brief, its task prompt or the Cockpit issues rules lose a rule, and
  when a shipped file names the removed routine, its key or the former label name.

### Adopting projects

- Delete the old cockpit wake task (the GitHub-triggered one, in claude.ai/code/routines).
- Re-do the setup with `routines/cockpit-command.md`: paste its brief into the project's main chat, then wire the
  API trigger into COCKPIT and press Test.
- The nightly bump removes the old `autonomy` key from `context/workflow.json`; nothing else to change by hand.

Install from npm: `npm i -D @softure-ai/skills@0.40.0`

Install from this release (no registry, no auth): `npm i -D https://github.com/SOFTURE/SKILLS/releases/download/v0.40.0/softure-ai-skills-0.40.0.tgz`

GitHub Packages: `@softure/skills@0.40.0` (requires a token with read:packages)
